# Neuroanatomy, Decerebrate Rigidity

**Authors:** Eric Whitney, Anthony J. Alastra

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Charles Sherrington was the first to describe decerebrate rigidity in 1898.  Also known as extensor posturing, decerebrate rigidity is a term that describes the involuntary extensor positioning of the arms, flexion of the hands, with knee extension and plantar flexion when stimulated as a result of a midbrain lesion. Decerebrate posturing is a tonic, static reflex that is maintained by the reticular formation and vestibulospinal system. The lesion is often in the midbrain between the red nuclei and lower vestibular nuclei; therefore, the remaining description will focus on the anatomy of the midbrain and related ascending and descending white matter tracts that lead to extensor posturing when damaged.
